isolation_mechanism: git worktree (NOT checkout -b in the dirty main tree)
why: The primary checkout /home/ubuntu has 20 modified tracked files and many untracked trees. A branch cut there would have absorbed unrelated dirty state into V8A, violating brief section 3.

code_isolation_proof.note: Repo modules hard-code sys.path.insert(0, '/home/ubuntu'). Because the first import of the `src` package binds src.__path__, a driver that inserts the worktree path and imports `src` first resolves ALL src.* submodules inside the worktree. Verified empirically for v6_prompt and corpus_adapter.

shared_untracked_dependencies.explanation: These are read through absolute /home/ubuntu paths and are NOT tracked by git, so the worktree necessarily reads the live main-tree copies. This is intended for EVIDENCE (the corpus is the data, not the code) but is recorded explicitly rather than left invisible.
